$comment: Vectors of the one builder (`ContributorPageBuilder`, design PROFILE-PAGE-2026-10-06 §3.6, §8.1) for a rule the public document cannot show: on a page without the login, no repository under the person's own GitHub account is listed or counted, because its group would print the login as the owner's name (schemas/contributor-page.v1.json `repositoriesSection`; contributor-page-settings.v1 check (j)). The document leaves out the very login the rule compares with, so neither schema can enforce it; this file is where the builder's tests (slice P14d) and check:contributor-page meet it.

`input` is the slice of the builder's inputs the rule reads: the person's current GitHub login, `showLogin`, the settings' `repositories` choice, and the credited repositories as the facts and the registry give them at this build (`owner` and `name` are the registry's). `expect` is either the repositories section (null when it has nothing to show and is not drawn), the two counts the summary takes from the same list (each printed only when switched on and not zero), and `leftOut`, every repository the rule removed with the code the editor shows beside it; or `{refused}`, the api's code at save.

Groups are in owner order and rows in name order (design §8.1). Every owner and name that is listed here is lower-case ASCII, and no two that are sorted together share a first letter, so any name order gives the same answer; the collation itself is the builder's.

`about` (1.2.0; ops decision D163): vectors of the one builder's about block, for the rules the public document cannot show alone: what it writes for the settings' `about` (schemas/contributor-page-settings.v1.json `about`) into the document's `about` (schemas/contributor-page.v1.json `about`). `input.about` is the settings' member; `input.textRules` is the text rules' answer to `ownText` at this build (`accepted` or `refused`; null where there are no words), which the builder asks Psn.PageSafety and this file states, as `credited` states the facts. `expect.about` is the document's member, or null when none is written. The tick off writes nothing; `own` with no words, or with words the rules now refuse, is written as `short`; the version is the settings' own, never stamped by the builder.

`cards` (1.3.0; ops decision D165): vectors of the one builder's cards member: what it writes for the settings' `cards` (schemas/contributor-page-settings.v1.json `cards`, stored with each member left out at its default and the member itself left out when all three are) into the document's `cards` (schemas/contributor-page.v1.json `cards`). `input.cards` is the settings' member, or null where the settings carry none (stored before 1.3.0, or every choice at its default); `expect.cards` is the document's member, which the builder writes on every document with all three members resolved. Which repository is the person's own is the renderer's reading of the document (its `login`), not the builder's.

`adopter` (1.4.0; ops decision D168 item 3): vectors of the one builder's licence adopter section, for the rules the public document cannot show alone: which repositories are listed and which years each item carries (schemas/contributor-page.v1.json `adopterSection`). `input.facts` are the builder's adopter facts in observed order, each with its repository's registry name, its evidence (`number` for `merged-pr`, `oid` for `direct-commit`, null where it has none), `registered` (the registry lists the repository at this build), `since` (the UTC year of the evidence's own date, null where none is stored) and `until` (the UTC year of the registry's recorded quit, which the callers pass for a repository that quit; null otherwise); `input.hidden` is the settings' `adopter.hidden`. `expect.adopter` is the section, or null when it has nothing to show. A registered repository is listed with `since` where it is known; one that left (not registered, with `until`) is listed only with both years, `since` no later than `until`; every other repository drops out.

`organisations` (1.5.0; ops decision D165 item 3, the organisation's picture): vectors of the one builder's judgment of which logins on a page are an organisation's, for the rule the public document cannot show: an organisation's copy (schemas/contributor-page.v1.json `$defs.organisationPicture`) is named only where GitHub's own answer, stored per repository, says so. `input.login` is the person's current GitHub login; `input.icon` the cards' icon, resolved; `input.shown` every repository the document shows, by the login it shows it under, the projects' groups first and then the licence adopter's items, each in its own order; `input.answers` the stored answers by repository (`ownerNodeId`, GitHub's node id of the owner; `ownerType`, GitHub's own `__typename`; `ownerLogin`, an organisation's login as GitHub answered, null for a user); `input.drawn` the organisations' copies the render job holds, by the owner's node id, each its `h16`. `expect.organisations` lists, in login order without regard to case, each login judged an organisation's, spelt as the page first shows it, with its owner's node id and the `h16` the document names on its every group and item, or null where no copy is drawn yet (the request side asks for it; the document names none). A login is an organisation's only while the cards' icon is `owner`, it is not the person's own, and every repository shown under it has an answer, each an `Organization`, all one owner, each under that login (compared without regard to case). Anything else draws the tile: a person's repository, an answer not yet read, two owners, a login that moved.

`listings` (1.5.0; ops decision D186 items 1 and 2): vectors of the one builder's listings member: what it writes for the settings' `listings` (schemas/contributor-page-settings.v1.json `listings`, stored with every member at its default left out, and a listing, or the member itself, left out when nothing is left) into the document's `listings` (schemas/contributor-page.v1.json `listings`). `input.listings` is the settings' member, or null where the settings carry none (stored before 1.5.0, or every choice at its default); `expect.listings` is the document's member, or null when none is written. Unlike `cards`, the builder writes only what differs from the defaults (the certificates `matrix`, the repositories `list`, no toggle on either), member by member, and leaves out a value the settings state at its default, so a page at the defaults carries no member and keeps its bytes. The renderer reads an absent member as its default.

`sponsorsPlacement` (settings 1.6.0, page 1.9.0; ops decision D189 and its dated note of 2026-10-29T10:0xZ): vectors of the one builder's `sponsorsPlacement`, where the support buttons show: what it writes for the settings' member (schemas/contributor-page-settings.v1.json `sponsorsPlacement`, `section` or `header`, stored only as `header`) into the document's (schemas/contributor-page.v1.json `sponsorsPlacement`, `header` alone). `input.sponsorsPlacement` is the settings' member, or null where the settings carry none (stored before 1.6.0, or at its default); `input.sponsorsOn` is the sponsors section's switch in the settings' `sections`. `expect.sponsorsPlacement` is the document's member, or null when none is written. As for `linksPlacement`, the builder writes it only as `header`, whatever the section's switch says (the switch decides whether the buttons show, the placement only where), and never `section`, so a page at the default carries no member and keeps its bytes. The renderer reads an absent member as `section`.

`certificates` (page 1.10.0; ops decision D202 items 1 and 2): vectors of the one builder's certificate listing, for the rule the public document cannot show: which of the person's own certificates the certificates section lists, in its order, and the summary's count (schemas/contributor-page.v1.json `certificatesSection`, WHAT IS LISTED). `input.showLogin` is whether the page shows the login, so the display it lists (`full` with it, `status-only` without); `input.mode` the settings' `certificates.mode`, with `selected` in the order chosen; `input.certificates` the person's certificate facts as the builder is handed them, each with its record's status, display, whether its holder put it On my page, the years its period names and, where the caller hands them over, the record's `validFrom` and `validUntil`. `expect.listed` is the ids the section lists, in its order (empty: no section), and `expect.certificates` the count the summary takes. The rule: only a `valid` certificate its holder put On my page, in the page's display and, by hand, chosen; of those only the ones whose period, by the months the item names (`months`: both dates handed over, in order and in their years), no other of them contains; of two equal periods the one with the greater id. A certificate that names no months is compared with none. Between them the vectors give the operator's dev case, each other status, a month inside all the time credited, a year beside an all-time certificate that does not contain it, an overlap without containment, two equal periods, three periods nested, a container off the page and one in the other display, both choices by hand, a period by its years alone and one whose dates contradict its years, a page without the login, and nothing to list.

`linksShow` (settings 1.7.0; ops decision D206 item 3): vectors of THE ONE RULE for what every link of a page shows, which the one builder (`ContributorPageSettings.LinksShowOf`) and the editor (`linksShowOf`) both run, and of what the builder writes from it. `input.settings` is the slice of the settings the rule reads, member for member as stored: `links` (each with its `show` where it carries one), `website` (null, or with its `show` where it carries one) and `linksShow` where the settings carry it. `input.neutral` is the logo record's answer at this build, which the builder asks Psn.PageSafety and this file states: the platforms whose brand's own rules refuse its logo on the page. `expect.linksShow` is the rule's answer, always all three members. `expect.items` is, per link in order, the `show` the builder writes on its item, or null where it writes none (all three); `expect.website` the `show` it writes on the website's item, or null where it writes none (both parts, or no website). The rule: `linksShow` where the settings carry it; else the first link's `show` (absent: all three), so an existing page keeps the look of its first link; else, with no link, the website's two parts with `handle` true for its domain; else the logo and the name, as a new page starts. The builder writes that one display on every link's item, with the name added on a `neutral` platform, and the website's item with its logo and name. The save refuses `linksShow` beside a per-link or website display, so no vector carries both.

`addNew` (settings 1.7.0; ops decisions D203 item 4 and D206 item 2; design D203-AUTO-LISTING-2026-11-09 §1, §6 and §8 item 3): vectors of the one rule `ContributorPageBuilder.AddNewDisplay`, which the yearly pass and the api ask and never re-derive: the display a new certificate starts On my page in, by the person's published page's setting, or null where it starts Private. `input.live` is the slice of the settings of the person's LIVE published version that the rule reads (`identity.showLogin`, `sections`, `certificates`, `repositories`), or null where the person has none (never published, hidden); never a draft. `input.login` is the person's current GitHub login, or null where none is known; `input.ageConfirmed` the stored 16-or-older tick of the page's first publish; `input.fullDisplayOpen` the plane's full-display switch; `input.certificateRepositoryIds` the node ids of the repositories the new certificate names. `expect.display` is `full`, `status-only` or null. The rule: null with no live version, unless the version carries `addNew: true` beside `mode: all-eligible`, with the Certificates section off, without the tick, or with full display closed; else `full` where the page shows a GitHub login (`identity.showLogin` and a login of the page schema's shape) and `status-only` where it does not; and null for a `full` certificate that names a repository the live `repositories` choice leaves out (in `hidden` in `all` mode, not among `selected` in `selected` mode), which the setting skips. The repositories section's own switch is not read: a `full` item names its projects whatever that switch says.

vectors.note: The login is hidden and the choice is `all`: the person's own `sam-codes/dotfiles` is left out of the section and of both counts, because its group would print the login; `other-org/invoice-kit` is the person's own hide.
The same person with "Show my login" on: the login is on the page anyway, so their own repository is listed under its owner like any other.
The login is hidden and the person selects their own repository by hand: the api refuses the save rather than leave out what was chosen in so many words.
GitHub logins are case-insensitive, so an owner the registry spells `Sam-Codes` is the person's own `sam-codes` and is left out; with `years` off no row carries its years.

Every credited repository is under the person's own account and the login is hidden: the section has nothing to show and is not drawn, and the summary counts no project. Without a certificate such a person can publish only with the login shown, and the editor says why.

about.note: The tick is off: no about block, whatever the variant; the choice is kept in the settings.
In my own words, with no words yet: the page shows our Short text until words exist (CW-38).
In my own words, with words a newer text rule refuses at a rebuild ("Purpose Source" followed by "team"): our Short text in their place, as a refused bio is left out.

about.ownText: Writing for the Purpose Source team here: we keep these tools free.

about.note: In my own words, accepted: the words exactly as stored.

about.ownText: Purpose Source lets my small libraries stay free for the people who need them most.

about.text: Purpose Source lets my small libraries stay free for the people who need them most.

about.note: Medium, with own words kept from an earlier choice: the words stay in the settings and never reach the document.

about.ownText: Purpose Source lets my small libraries stay free for the people who need them most.

cards.note: No `cards` in the settings (stored before 1.3.0, or every choice at its default): the builder writes the three defaults, the owner's icon, an own repository by its name alone, another owner's as owner/name.
The GitHub mark alone chosen: the two name choices are written at their defaults.
No icon, an own repository as owner/name and another owner's by its name alone: every member chosen, each written as chosen.
Another owner's repositories by their name alone: the owner's icon and the own name form are written at their defaults.
Own repositories as owner/name: written so, the other members at their defaults.
The defaults stated by a client (the api stores none of them): the same document as BC-1.

adopter.note: A registered repository whose evidence date is stored: its item carries `since`, the UTC year of the pull request's merge ("Since 2026").
Registered, with no evidence date stored (a fact from before 1.4.0, until the person's next check dates it): the item carries no year, never a guessed one.
LEFT: the person merged the licence in 2026 and the repository quit (FS-02 T5) in 2027, recorded: it stays listed with both years, `since` 2026 and `until` 2027, drawn "2026–2027".
Left within one year (a commit of 2027, a quit of 2027): both members are written, and the renderer draws the one year.

Not registered, and no `until`: a delisting (T7), a suspension, a quit the registry recorded no date for (a repository imported from registry-v0), or a repository gone from the registry otherwise. None is a leave of the licence the page can date, so the item drops out, as before 1.4.0, and with nothing left the section is not drawn.

A repository that quit, recorded in 2027, whose evidence date is not stored: `until` is never written alone, so the item drops out until the person's next check dates its evidence; the registered repository beside it stays.

A quit recorded before the evidence (the licence merged again in 2028 into a repository the registry still records as quit since 2027, before any restore): `until` would precede `since`, so the item drops out.

Registered again after a quit (T8's restore): the item carries `since` alone. Its callers pass no `until` for a registered repository, and were one passed (the quit before the restore), the builder still writes none: only a left item carries one.

The person's own hide drops a repository, left or not; a fact whose evidence the renderer could not rebuild (a merged pull request with no number) is never an item; and of two facts on one repository the first in observed order is its item, with that fact's own year, so the year always dates the evidence the item links to.

organisations.note: An organisation answered for every repository the page shows under its login, its copy drawn: judged, with the copy's `h16`, which the document names on the group. `sam-codes` is answered a `User`, another person: never judged, whatever is drawn, and its card keeps the tile.

Answered an organisation, but the render job holds no copy yet: judged (the request side asks for its picture), with no `h16`, so the document names none and the card draws the tile until the copy exists.
The cards' icon is `github`: no leading picture is drawn, so no login is judged, whatever the answers, and nothing is named, asked for or copied.

One repository under the login has no answer yet (credited since the last read): the login is not judged until every repository the page shows under it is answered, and its cards keep the tile meanwhile.
Two answers under one login name two owners (a repository moved, and the registry has not followed yet): not judged, so no picture can stand for the wrong account.

The answer's login is not the login the page shows (the organisation was renamed after the registry last named it, or before the answer was read): not judged, so a stale answer can only fall back to the tile.
The page owner's own login is never judged, whatever an answer says: an own repository keeps the page's own picture, and a person's own account is never shown as an organisation's.

One login shown in the projects and in the licence adopter's sections, every answer the same organisation: one entry, its copy named on the group and on the item alike; and an organisation shown in the adopter section alone, judged as well.
Case is folded, as everywhere a login is compared: the page shows `Example-Org` (the registry's spelling) and GitHub answers `example-org`; the entry keeps the page's spelling.

listings.note: No `listings` in the settings (stored before 1.5.0, or every choice at its default): the builder writes none, and the page draws the certificates as a matrix and the repositories as a list, with no toggle.
The certificates as a list, nothing else chosen: only that member is written.
The repositories' toggle alone: they open as the list, their default, and visitors may switch them.
The certificates' toggle and the repositories as a matrix: one member of each listing.
All four values other than their defaults: written as they are.
Defaults stated beside a choice (an input form the api never stores, since it leaves defaults out): the builder leaves each default out, and the certificates' listing with it.
Every value stated at its default: nothing is left, so no member is written, as for BL-1.

sponsorsPlacement.note: Stored `header`, the sponsors section on: written, and the buttons and the fixed line under them stand together with the name.
`section` stated (an input form the api never stores, since it leaves the default out): nothing is written, and the buttons stand in their own section.
No `sponsorsPlacement` in the settings (stored before 1.6.0, or at its default): nothing is written, and the page draws the buttons in their own section, as before.

Stored `header` with the sponsors section off: still written, as `linksPlacement` is whatever the links section's switch says. The switch decides that no button shows; the placement only says where they would.

certificates.note: The operator's dev case: February, February–March, February–April revoked, February–May superseded, February–May valid and February–June, all On my page with the login shown. The revoked and the superseded ones are never listed (item 1), and February–June contains every other valid one (item 2): one card, the longest.
Valid only (item 1): four periods no other contains, one valid, one expired, one revoked and one superseded. The valid one alone is listed and counted.
A month inside all the time credited: the all-time certificate alone.
A year's certificate beside an all-time one that starts in its February, so contains no January: neither contains the other, and both are listed, newest years first.
Two periods that overlap without one containing the other (February–May and April–July): both listed, by their ids.
Two certificates of one period, which one live certificate per person and period rules out: the newer, the greater id, alone.
A month inside its year's certificate, both inside all the time credited from January: the all-time one alone.
A longer certificate its holder has not put On my page hides nothing: the month alone is listed.
A longer certificate in the display the page does not show (status-only on a page that shows the login) is not listed and hides nothing.
Chosen by hand: an all-time certificate the person did not choose hides nothing, and the chosen are listed in the order chosen.
Chosen by hand, the all-time certificate among them: it hides the chosen month it contains, and the rest keep the order chosen.

A certificate whose record's dates were not handed over names its years alone and is compared with none: it stays beside an all-time certificate its years would fit in, which still hides a dated month.
Dates that contradict the years the record names (an end in 2027 for a certificate of 2026) name no months, so that certificate is compared with none.
A page without the login lists status-only certificates, nested as on any page; a full one is not listed and hides nothing.
Nothing valid: a revoked, a superseded and an expired certificate, the longest revoked. Nothing is listed or counted, and no section is drawn.

linksShow.note: The settings carry `linksShow`, the logo alone: every link's item is written with it, and the website's item with its logo and without the word "Website". Its domain always shows.
The settings carry `linksShow` with all three parts, which the api stores as stated: the builder writes no `show` on any item and none on the website, as it leaves every display out at all three.

Stored before 1.7.0 with three looks: the first link the logo alone, the second with no display of its own, the third the logo and the name, and the website with neither part. An existing page keeps the look of its first link: every item is written with the logo alone, and the website follows it.
Stored before 1.7.0, the first link with no display of its own (all three), the second the logo alone: all three for every link, so no `show` is written.
No link, and a website that shows the word "Website" without the globe: the rule's answer is the website's two parts and its domain, and the website's item keeps what it had.
No link, and a website with no display of its own (both parts): all three, and nothing is written.
No link and no website: the logo and the name, which is how a new page's links start (ops decision D206 item 3). Nothing is drawn yet; the editor writes this answer at the first link added.

`linksShow` is the logo alone and the list holds GitLab, whose own rules do not let a page show its logo: GitLab's item is written with its name too, whatever the choice says, and the other link as chosen. The save never refuses `linksShow` for it.
`linksShow` is the username alone, beside GitLab and a website: GitLab's item shows its name and the username, the other link the username, and the website its domain alone.

Stored before 1.7.0, the first link GitLab with the logo and the username, stored before its brand refused its logo: the rule's answer is that stored look, the second link is written with it, and GitLab's item with its name added, which makes all three, so none is written on it.
No link, and a website that shows neither the globe nor the word: its domain alone, and the website's item keeps what it had.
`linksShow` is the logo and the name, with a website and no link: the website's item shows both parts, so nothing is written.

addNew.note: The published page lists all eligible certificates, shows its Certificates section and the GitHub login, and carries `addNew: true`; the 16-or-older tick is stored and full display is open: the new certificate starts On my page in `full`.
The same page without the login: the new certificate starts On my page in `status-only`, without the name or projects.
`identity.showLogin` is on but no GitHub login is known at this build, so the page shows none: `status-only`, the display the page has.
No live version (never published, hidden, or taken down): the setting is not in effect, and the certificate starts Private.
The person switched it off and published: nothing is added.
A version published before 1.7.0 carries no `addNew`: the rule does not act on it, though the editor shows the switch on. It acts from the next publish, whose confirmation states it.
The page lists certificates chosen by hand (`selected`), which never stands beside `addNew`: nothing is added.
The published page does not show its Certificates section: nothing is added.
No stored 16-or-older tick for the person's page: nothing is added.
Full display is closed on this plane: nothing is added.
Full display is closed, on a page without the login: nothing is added either; the setting acts only while full display is open.
The new certificate names a project the page hides (`repositories.hidden`): the setting skips it, and it starts Private (design §8 item 3).
The page lists projects chosen by hand, and the new certificate names one that is not among them: skipped.
The page lists projects chosen by hand, and every project the new certificate names is among them: `full`.
A page without the login whose `repositories` choice hides a project the certificate names: `status-only`. A status-only item shows no project, so nothing is skipped.
The new certificate names no repository: `full`.
In `selected` mode `hidden` is not read, as the builder does not read it there: a project both selected and hidden is listed, and the certificate starts `full`.
